key_insight: GRADE is the first benchmark to measure discipline-informed knowledge and reasoning in image editing, using 520 curated samples across 10 academic domains to expose where multimodal models fail under structured, domain-specific constraints.
problem_solved: Existing image-editing benchmarks are limited to natural images and shallow commonsense tasks, so they don't evaluate a model's ability to apply domain knowledge and structured reasoning when making semantically and procedurally correct edits.
method: Curated dataset: 520 samples spanning 10 academic disciplines, each paired with domain-constrained editing tasks and expert annotations.
Task design: Edit prompts and evaluation criteria formulated to require discipline-specific knowledge and multi-step reasoning beyond generic commonsense.
Evaluation protocol: Standardized metrics and per-domain analyses to benchmark multimodal models' ability to perform correct, discipline-informed edits.
impact: GRADE provides a practical testbed for diagnosing and improving multimodal models' domain reasoning in image editing, guiding dataset creation, model training, and evaluation for applications that require discipline-aware visual manipulation.
visual_elements: Pie chart or stacked bar showing dataset composition: 10 domains and sample counts (520 total).

Pipeline flowchart illustrating dataset curation, task formulation, annotation, and evaluation metrics.
paper_title: GRADE: Benchmarking Discipline-Informed Reasoning in Image Editing
paper_authors: Mingxin Liu, Ziqian Fan, Zhaokai Wang, Leyao Gu, Zirun Zhu
